messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [P1] High error rate on deployment 'inference-canary-3' (v2026.03.17). Multiple pods CrashLoopBackOff on node-3, HPA oscillating between 0->3 replicas, rollout still in progress. Affected endpoint: /v1/generate (eu-west). Oncall: @maria-oncall

maria-oncall: got the page, jumping in. can someone paste recent pod logs?

drew-sre: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep inference-canary-3` shows 3 pods on node-3, restarts 5-10. Events show LivenessProbe failures then OOMKilled on the model-loader container. pasting kube events:
```
Type     Reason     Age   From               Message
----     ------     ----  ----               -------
Warning  BackOff    2m    kubelet, node-3    Back-off restarting failed container
Warning  OOMKilled  2m    kubelet, node-3    Container killed due to memory usage
```

maria-oncall: memory spike in model-loader during startup — looks like this build/flag pulled a larger model variant. is this related to the canary config change in this rollout?

kate-support: support seeing a spike in 502s from EU customers, roughly ~12% of requests failing in last 5m, high latency for interactive customers. no major customer-facing alerts yet but some merchants reported degraded experiences.

maria-oncall: okay prioritize stopping rollout and getting traffic off these pods. tom, can you pause the rollout in CI / flip the feature flag?

tom-eng: pausing rollout now. also flipping the canary-serving flag to false to force fallback to stable model. command I ran (LaunchDarkly):
```
ldctl toggle --env=prod --flag=canary_serving --off --comment "incident: crashloop on inference-canary-3"
```

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline v2026.03.17 pause requested by tom-eng — pausing canary.

maria-oncall: removing pods from service mesh and cordoning node-3 to avoid further scheduling pressure:
```
kubectl cordon node-3
kubectl delete pod -l app=inference-canary-3 -n inference
```

drew-sre: after delete, new pods are being scheduled but HPA still sees CPU burst from pending restarts. short-term mitigation: scaling down HPA minReplicas to 0 for canary so it doesn't keep trying to spin up failing pods:
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-canary-3-hpa -n inference --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":0}}'
```

maria-oncall: done. traffic should stop hitting canary; routing layer fallback to stable model variant triggered by flag. kate, can you confirm customer error rate dropping?

kate-support: error rate falling — 502s down from 12% to ~1.8% in EU after flag flip and cordon. still seeing residual errors from in-flight requests. notifying top impacted merchants.

drew-sre: root cause hypothesis: manifest change in v2026.03.17 enabled a new model variant without updated resource requests/limits -> memory blowup on startup. also noticed node-3 had a recent kernel OOM event during a drain earlier today which may have less memory headroom.

maria-oncall: we should rollback the deployment artifact and revert the manifest in git. I'll kick rollout undo and create a post-deploy job to validate resource profiles.

maria-oncall: running rollback:
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-canary-3 -n inference --to-revision=3
```

deploy-bot: Rollback started for deployment inference-canary-3 to revision 3. Canary paused.

drew-sre: also capturing diagnostics: `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl logs --previous` from crashlooping pods, uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-incidents/3211112222/diagnostics.log

maria-oncall: handing off to drewsre for post-incident investigation and suggested fix (resource requests + guard on model variant pull). im going to update status and start an incident page. assigning follow-ups: drewsre (root cause & fix), tom-eng (CI gating to prevent model-variant without resource bump), kate-support (customer comms & impact summary).

kate-support: drafting customer note now, will include ETA for full mitigation and expressed remediation steps. estimated customer downtime window: 9m from first page to rollback stable. impacted % of EU traffic peak ~12%.

drew-sre: quick actionable items: 1) add admission webhook check that disallows model-size changes without resource updates, 2) increase default mem limit for model-loader container, 3) investigate node-3 memory health and schedule remediation.

maria-oncall: agreed. logging this as P1 incident. I'll escalate to oncall-sre rotation for postmortem. great job to everyone for rapid mitigation :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident recorded: id INC-2026-3211112222. paging history attached. next steps: postmortem in #postmortems, oncall handoff to drewsre for RCA.
